simple.meaning: אָדַר (ʼâdar) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to expand , i.e. be great or (figuratively) magnificent.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 3 times in Exodus, Isaiah, beginning at Exodus 15:6. The surrounding contexts include righteousness, Torah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אָדַר (H142) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: אָדַר (ʼâdar) / H142 is traced through Exodus 15:6, Exodus 15:11, Isaiah 42:21 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: to expand , i.e. be great or (figuratively) magnificent
definitions.full: H142. adar [ אָדַר ] verb (poetry) wide, great , (thence) high, noble (? Assyrian adâru Dl W ) — Niph`al Participle majestic, glorious , of נֶאְדָּר ׳י, Exod 15:11 ; construct נֶאְדָּרִי 15:6 (see Di); Hiph`il Imperfect יַאְדִּיר make glorious the teaching Isa 42:21 ( ׳י subject)

occurrences.englishText: Your right hand, Yahweh, is glorious in power.
Who is like you, Yahweh, among the gods?
It pleased Yahweh, for his righteousness’ sake, to magnify the law
